# Apollo Advising

> Apollo Advising (Apollo RE Advising LLC) has two practices, both billed by the hour. AI for business: one-on-one AI training and implementation with founder Denver McClure, an owner who runs his own companies on AI every day, for business owners, home service companies, real estate investors, and property managers (CRM, lead generation and follow-up, after-hours phones, reporting on the numbers, admin, and team training). Real estate decisions: independent analysis for rental property owners deciding whether to buy, hold, sell, refinance, change rental strategy, or pursue a 1031 exchange. Denver is a Marine Corps veteran and active Texas landlord.

## Key facts
- AI for business: $299 per hour by Zoom or phone. In person within 50 miles of Dallas: $1,249 half day (up to 4 hours) or $1,999 full day (up to 8 hours), booked at least one week ahead. On site elsewhere: $2,499 per day plus travel and lodging at cost, booked at least two weeks ahead. Details at https://www.apolloadvising.com/ai/ and https://www.apolloadvising.com/pricing/
- Ownership: clients own everything built. Tools are built in the client's own accounts; Denver does not hold client data or tools on his own computers and does not keep copies.
- AI scope: AI sessions are training and implementation help with AI tools and workflows. They are not financial, investment, tax, legal, or accounting advice, and not advice on how to run or invest in your business. They are not connected to Denver McClure's other companies, and you are never asked to use any of them.
- Pricing: $299 per hour, or $799 for a three-hour block used within 12 months. Time is billed in 15-minute increments. The first 30-minute call is free.
- Written option, no call needed: a Rental Property Analysis Report on one property, $99 for a PDF within 2 business days or $149 for rush delivery within 1 business day, with a code for 50% off the first one-hour strategy session, good for 30 days after delivery. Order at https://www.apolloadvising.com/property-analysis/
- Sessions are by phone or Zoom, nationwide. Book at https://www.apolloadvising.com/book/
- Scope: real property and business operations only. Apollo Advising does not provide legal, tax, investment, insurance, or lending advice, and does not advise on securities such as Delaware Statutory Trusts (DSTs), REITs, TIC interests, private placements, or syndications.
- Investment advice is offered only through Nashional Independent Investment Management LLC, a separate registered investment adviser.
- Local focus: based in McKinney, Texas, serving Dallas, Collin, Denton, and Tarrant counties, plus clients nationwide.
- Contact: denver@apolloadvising.com

## Short answers
- Should I sell my rental property or keep it? Compare keeping, selling, and exchanging side by side, starting with return on equity: annual net cash flow divided by market value minus loan balance. Example: a $450,000 rental with a $150,000 loan netting $9,000 a year earns 3% on its $300,000 of equity, before appreciation and loan paydown.
- What are the 1031 exchange deadlines? 45 days after the sale closes to identify replacement property in writing, and 180 days to close (sooner if the tax return is due first, unless extended). A qualified intermediary must hold the proceeds.
- Airbnb, medium-term, or long-term rental? Compare net income after all costs and the time each takes. Short-term usually has the highest gross and highest costs; furnished stays of 30+ days often land in between.
- Does Apollo Advising give investment advice? No. Investment advice is offered only through Nashional Independent Investment Management LLC, a separate registered investment adviser.

It can watch your website forms, social messages, and phone line, reply within minutes with an accurate first answer, ask the qualifying questions, and log every lead in your CRM. Denver sets this up with you in your own accounts and teaches you to run it.
- [A CRM built from scratch](https://www.apolloadvising.com/ai/crm/): Yes. With current AI tools, a small business can build a working CRM around its own sales process in days rather than months: pipeline stages, contact records, reminders, follow-up, and reports. Denver builds it with you in accounts you own, so you are not locked into his systems or a long software contract.
- [Website and follow-up](https://www.apolloadvising.com/ai/website-and-follow-up/): AI can now build most of a small business website: the pages, the copy drafts, the structure search engines and AI assistants read, and the forms. A person still needs to check every claim and make the design decisions. Denver builds the site with you, connects it to your CRM and follow-up, and hands you the keys.
- [Financial reporting](https://www.apolloadvising.com/ai/financial-reporting/): Yes, for operating reports. AI tools can pull figures from accounting software and your CRM, assemble a one-page summary of revenue, receivables, pipeline, and job status, and email it to you on a set schedule. Your CPA still handles tax and accounting. Denver builds the reports with you so you can read and trust every number.
- [A team of AI agents](https://www.apolloadvising.com/ai/ai-agents/): An AI agent is software that can take a series of steps toward a goal with your permission, such as checking your CRM each morning, summarizing what changed, drafting follow-ups, and flagging problems. A team of agents splits that work into roles. Denver sets them up with you, with clear limits on what each one may do and a person approving anything that goes to customers.
- [AI for home service businesses](https://www.apolloadvising.com/ai/home-service-businesses/): Home service companies win on speed and follow-through, and that is where AI helps first: answering calls and messages after hours, replying to every lead within minutes, keeping the CRM current, reminding the team about stalled jobs, requesting reviews, and sending the owner a short report on the numbers. Denver runs his own service business this way and sets it up with you.
- [AI for real estate investors](https://www.apolloadvising.com/ai/real-estate-investors/): Investors use AI to screen deals faster, draft and organize tenant and owner communication, track maintenance and leases, and produce portfolio reports without manual spreadsheets. Denver is an active Texas landlord who uses these tools himself. Sessions are training and implementation help with AI tools, not investment advice.
- [AI in Dallas-Fort Worth](https://www.apolloadvising.com/ai/dallas-fort-worth/): Yes. Denver McClure works in person within 50 miles of Dallas, including Collin, Dallas, Denton, and Tarrant counties. A half day is $1,249 and a full day is $1,999, booked at least one week ahead. Hourly sessions by Zoom are $299. Apollo Advising is based in McKinney, Texas.
- [How to start using AI in a small business](https://www.apolloadvising.com/guides/how-to-start-using-ai-in-a-small-business/): Start with one costly, repetitive task, not a company-wide rollout. For most owners that is lead response, follow-up, or a weekly report. Set it up in accounts you own, keep a person approving anything customers see, measure the time it saves for a month, then add the next task.
- [What is an AI agent, and does my business need one?](https://www.apolloadvising.com/guides/what-is-an-ai-agent/): An AI agent is AI software that can take several steps toward a goal using tools you give it access to, such as reading your CRM, checking an inbox, drafting a reply, or updating a record. A chatbot answers a question; an agent works through a task. Most small businesses benefit from agents that monitor and draft, with a person approving the final step.
